statement: For every pair of integers m>=2,n>=1 and every integer 1<=k<=n, let W^(m)_(n,k)(t) sum t^nne(D) over all N=(0,1),E=(1,0) paths from (0,0) to (n,mn) whose every prefix satisfies #N>=m#E and which have exactly k consecutive NE factors; nne(D) counts consecutive NNE factors, without cyclic counting. Then W^(m)_(n,k)(t)=(binom(n,k)/n)*sum_{j=1}^k binom(k,j)*binom(mn-k,j-1)*t^j. This polynomial has degree k, a simple root at 0, and k-1 distinct strictly negative roots, so every complex zero is real, proving the complete assertion of source.md.
contribution: An explicit enumeration identifies the fixed-peak Fuss NNE distribution with a positive scalar multiple of the known ordinary-Dyck polynomial V_(mn+1,k), resolving the precisely frozen Fuss assertion. A self-contained Rodrigues argument also proves root simplicity. The ordinary theorem, first-return method, Lagrange inversion, and Jacobi theory are known and credited. No equivalent Fuss identification or resolution was found in the bounded primary-source comparison on 2026-09-12; global priority is not asserted.
